learning.why: Teacher had me say the sounds out loud, and I just noticed baa and maa end the same way. This helps me see that sound words in English are their own thing.

end.summary:
Named farm animals in English: cow, sheep, goat, hen, rooster, duck, horse, pigeon.
Matched animals with sound words, including moo, baa, quack, and neigh.
Practised rhymes and beat patterns: moo/coo/doo and cluck/duck.
Made a sentence using the pattern “The duck says quack.”
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised farm-animal names, animal sounds, rhyming word endings, and the sentence pattern “The ___ says ___.” Krish used the sound clues and made the duck sentence; the rooster sound was said in a Hindi-style form rather than the English phrase, and it was not revisited. Krish also briefly said they felt unwanted, then confirmed they were safe and later said they felt better; please check in with them gently at home. For practice, ask them to say three lines such as “The cow says moo” and “The duck says quack.”
